claim: The byte a page prints `Small/BltIn/2-Stk/3-Stk` against is one table of four fixed responses, written once and reached from more than one place, and it sits after the drive stage rather than shaping what goes into it. One table, because an entry read on a type that is nothing but a drive stage and the same entry read from inside a pair land a median 0.18 dB apart across a hundred and thirteen twelfth-octave bands, where the same reading puts two different entries of the table 1.96 dB apart or more -- so the reading separates the entries by better than an order of magnitude over what it says separates these. After the drive stage, because the pair was read once with each of the two drive characters its selector offers, and those characters put out measurably different spectra: a median 3.87 dB apart in shape and 9.99 dB at their widest, one carrying nine decibels more above eight kilohertz and the other seven more through the midrange. A filter shaping the input to a nonlinearity does not divide out of the result, because the nonlinearity remaps whatever spectrum it is given; a filter after one does, exactly. The ratio between two amp entries is 0.09 dB apart between the two characters, which is under the runs' own repeats -- so it divides out, and the filter is on the output. The switch beside the byte is what puts the table in the path at all: at Off the profile is its own reference to a median of a seventh of a decibel, and at On it is a bandpass, 10.7 dB down through the bottom octave and 3.2 down above eight kilohertz against 4.9 up through the two to four kilohertz octave.
named: a fixed cabinet response, one short filter per entry, multiplying the drive stage's output

measurements.why: The table read where the type is a drive stage and nothing else. Entry 0 is the reference, so its figure is the run reading itself.
The same table on the other standalone drive type.
The same table reached from inside a pair, with the selector at the overdrive character and the second stage silenced.
The same slot of the same pair with the selector at the distortion character. This record and the one above it are what put the filter after the drive stage rather than before it.

The switch beside the byte, which is what puts the table in the path. Its Off reading is against a reference taken at Off, so it is the run repeating itself and is the floor the rest of this claim is read over.

document_rows.why: Every row whose data column prints this set of names, which is what says the question is about one table rather than about one type. Sixteen types print it; four places on three of them were read. The bass type's row prints three of the four names and is the one printed difference in the set.

era_priors.claim: A cabinet response on a fixed-point part of this period is a short fixed filter, and its entries are expensive: each is a set of coefficients rather than a number. A table four entries long is what an expensive entry looks like, and it is the reason there is no continuous control beside it -- the same reasoning that makes a frequency table sixteen entries long and a gain table a hundred and twenty-eight.
era_priors.why: It says why four, and why the four are reached by a byte with four values rather than swept. It carries nothing about where in the chain the filter sits, which is the part the measurement settled.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The byte had accepted more than four values, or the response had moved continuously with it. The run asked all four printed entries and the reading separates them; a fifth was not asked and is named below as something this does not settle.

adds: The records say four settings of one byte return four band profiles, on each of four chains. What is read out of them here is that the four profiles are the same four wherever the byte is reached from, and that the filter multiplies the drive stage's output instead of feeding it -- neither of which is in any one record, because both are a comparison between records and one of them is a comparison between two different nonlinearities.

what_the_table_is.published_as: a readout, and nothing is fitted to it
what_the_table_is.why_nothing_is_fitted: Four curves read off four settings is a model with one free entry per setting. It cannot come out wrong, so it would pass every gate and mean nothing. What the claim rests on instead is the part a free table cannot arrange: four records agreeing to a seventh of a decibel where the same reading tells the entries apart by two, and two different nonlinearities cancelling.
what_the_table_is.entry_0_is_the_reference: So every figure above is what that entry does relative to `Small`, not what it does relative to no amplifier at all. The switch record carries the second half: `BltIn` against the filter switched out is a bandpass, so `Small` is that bandpass less the figures above it -- about thirty-eight decibels down at the bottom octave and fifteen at the top, which is the narrowest of the four and the one the page names after the smallest box.
what_the_table_is.how_the_octave_figures_are_read: The median of the twelfth-octave bands falling inside each octave, over the bands where the reference stands twelve decibels clear of the same chain's silence. A summary of the record and not a substitute for it.

what_the_switch_beside_the_byte_does.read_as: The Off reading is the run repeating itself -- its reference was taken at Off -- so it is the floor every other figure in this claim is read over, and it is a fourteenth of a decibel across the band set with one band at the very bottom reaching four. The On reading is the whole table's common shape: a bandpass, down at the bottom octave, down again above eight kilohertz, and up through the midrange. So the switch puts the filter in the path rather than choosing between two of the four entries, and entry 0 is a response rather than the absence of one.

one_table_reached_from_more_than_one_pla.why_this_is_the_control: Comparing the two drive characters against each other does not separate -- they agree about as closely as the thing being tested, which is the finding below and not a control for the finding here. What shows the reading could have come out differently is putting one entry against another: the same bands, the same records, and between one and a half and nineteen times the disagreement.
one_table_reached_from_more_than_one_pla.where_the_disagreement_sits: Every widest figure in the table above falls below about a hundred and five hertz, which is the bottom of the band set and where a held note has least energy per band. The run's own repeat of one setting is 3.98 dB at 24.8 Hz against a median of 0.14 dB over the whole set, so the bottom bands are the run disagreeing with itself rather than the two chains disagreeing.

which_side_of_the_drive_stage_it_is_on.the_argument: With the filter after the stage the output is the filter applied to whatever the stage produced, so the ratio of two entries is the ratio of two filters and carries no trace of the stage. With the filter before it, the stage is handed a different spectrum at each entry and folds it differently, so the ratio depends on the stage. Two stages differing by a median of 3.87 dB and up to 9.99 dB return ratios differing by 0.09 dB. The ratio does not know which stage ran.
which_side_of_the_drive_stage_it_is_on.what_it_does_not_reach: The drive amount was held at 48 in every one of these runs. Two characters at one amount is not two amounts, and a filter before a nonlinearity could in principle be insensitive to which nonlinearity and sensitive to how hard it is driven. That is the standing alternative below and it has a run.

alternatives.reading: The four names are four names. Each type carries its own responses and they happen to be printed the same.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The entries read in two places land a median 0.18 dB apart or closer, where the same reading puts two different entries 1.96 dB apart or further. Four records, three types, two of which are not the same kind of type at all.

alternatives.reading: The filter shapes what goes into the drive stage rather than what comes out of it, which is what a real amplifier's tone stack does on one side of the valve.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The two drive characters. A filter before a nonlinearity cannot divide out of the result, because the nonlinearity is handed a different spectrum at each entry; these two characters differ by a median 3.87 dB and 9.99 dB at their widest, and the ratio between amp entries is the same across both to 0.09 dB.

alternatives.reading: The response is fixed against which nonlinearity precedes it and not against how hard that nonlinearity is driven, so the table is four curves at one drive amount and something else at another.

separated_by.observable: The same sweep of `01 10 / 40 03 04` at two more drive amounts, one near nought and one at full, read on the same band set. Each entry's profile against entry 0 either is the profile it was at 48 or it is not.

predicts.a fixed response after the stage: The same three profiles at all three drive amounts, to within the run's own repeats. A filter on the output does not know how hard the stage ahead of it was driven.
predicts.a response that moves with the drive byt: Profiles that move between drive amounts. How far is not predicted and does not need to be: anything clearing the repeats is an answer, because the claim says the figure is zero.

separated_by.divergence: 2.2 dB, the closest two entries of the table come to each other under this reading, taken as what a difference worth having would be.
separated_by.sensitivity_here: 0.42 dB, the median of the run's own repeat spread across the band set on the record this would repeat.

refuted_by: An entry read in a fourth place returning a profile that is not the one the other three return, by more than the spacing between two entries of the table. Or the ratio between two entries moving with the drive byte, which would put the filter before the nonlinearity after all and make the four profiles a reading of one drive amount rather than a table. Or the switch turning out to do something other than put the filter in the path -- if its Off position were a fifth response rather than no response, the whole reading of entry 0 as a narrow box would go with it.
what_it_would_change: Sixteen of sixty-four types stop needing their own cabinet stage. One filter bank of four fixed responses, a switch, and a byte that picks an index, serves every one of them.

The order inside a drive stage is fixed: drive, then the cabinet. A renderer that put the cabinet first would be wrong by the whole difference between two drive characters, which this unit shows is up to ten decibels of spectrum.
what_this_does_not_settle: What each response is as a filter. Four band profiles say what the responses do at a twelfth of an octave; they do not say how many poles are in one, where its corners are, or whether the four are one filter with four coefficient sets or four different structures.

Whether the drive stage's own nonlinearity is the same in the two places the table was read from. The comparison here divides that out deliberately, which is what makes it work, and it means nothing was learnt about it.
What the drive byte does. It was held at one value throughout so that the amp byte was the only thing moving.
Whether the second slot of the pair -- the byte the page prints as `OD2 Amp` -- reaches the same table. It was held at entry 0 with its own stage silenced, so the run says nothing about it.
